title: Who is a Watsi ambassador?
headline: A Watsi ambassador is anyone who finds their own way to bring Watsi into their life. Four real people, four different ways, no script.
story: The question comes first, on screen: who is a Watsi ambassador? Kat's answer: someone who found their own way to bring Watsi into their life. Then four real people: Reena (storytelling and Roll Call), Daniel (a student chapter), Sydney (field visits and companies), Linnea (the volunteer community).
It ends warm and open: there isn't a script you have to follow. Bring Watsi into your world in a way that feels like you. Not a recruitment ad: no sign-up, no form, no urgency.
do: Open on frame 1 with the question typed on screen and Kat already on camera.
Then a straight cut into her answer. Question first, answer second.
Keep captions on the whole time, Lato, large. One text at a time.
Name super “Kat” only, large, after the question has landed.
Put each ambassador's first name on screen as she says it: Reena · Daniel · Sydney · Linnea.
dont: Don't open on Kat saying hello or on a logo.
Don't use the false starts, “sorry” lines or prompter chat. Only the takes named below.
Don't speed-ramp her voice. Trim breaths and pauses instead.
Don't make Daniel the spine. He is one of four names, said once.

bp_intro: Kat reads Sonam's Script 2 from a prompter in three takes (C5061–C5063). Only the clean takes below are used. Source times come from the transcript and are accurate to about 1 s. Output times are estimated from her reading speed: set the real ones on the waveform.

rows.visual: Use the seconds just before her first word (C5061 00:34–00:38): Kat on camera, settled, no talking. Pick the frame on scrub. Mute the audio under the question. Crop centered on her face.
rows.motion: The question types on, frame 1: Who is a Watsi ambassador? Bold, Watsi yellow #FFCC33, Lato Bold (or September Spirit if it reads as well; Lato is safer). Large, upper half. It is the title and the thumbnail. It stays up while she starts her answer, at least 5 s in total.
rows.sfx: Room tone. No whoosh, no typing sound.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.
rows.motion: Question text stays up to 00:05, then out. Captions start. Her first line repeats the question: the question text works as its caption. Name super “Kat” at 00:04–00:06, lower left, above the captions, large. First name only.

voice.quote: So who is a Watsi ambassador? I think of it as someone who has found their own way of bringing Watsi into the rest of their life.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.
rows.motion: Name beat: “Reena” as she says it, then captions. Captions: Roll Call · Collective H'Art (script doc spellings).

voice.quote: Reena brings Watsi into storytelling. She hosts Roll Call with our community and she shares patient stories and helped create our very first in-person Watsi art event called the Collective H'Art.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: Daniel started a Watsi chapter at Stony Brook when he was a student back at college and it has continued to bring Watsi into universities and classrooms and into communities, all that he's a part of.
voice.src: C5061 01:08–01:24 (cut before “Sorry” at 01:25; alternate take C5062 00:00–00:13)

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.
rows.motion: Name beat: “Sydney”, then captions. Find the in-point on scrub: the transcript merges the two takes.

voice.quote: Sydney has brought Watsi into field visits, storytelling and conversations with companies, including helping us think about things like matching gifts.
voice.src: C5062 ≈00:31–00:49 (second take; the first take says “donor matching gifts”: don't use it)

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: Linnea has helped build our volunteer community and has brought ideas around things like giving with kids and families into the conversation.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: There are a lot of different ways to be a part of this. Maybe you love telling stories. Maybe you're the person who gets people together. Maybe you want to bring Watsi into your university or your workplace or your community or your place of worship. Maybe you have an idea we haven't thought of yet.

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: That's what I like about being a Watsi ambassador. There isn't a script that you have to follow. It's really about taking something you care about and finding a way to share it with the people around you.
voice.src: C5063 01:30–01:39 (third take; the takes at 00:41 and 00:54 break)

rows.visual: Kat at the prompter. Same set-up. Hide jump cuts between script blocks with a 3–5% push-in, not a wipe.

voice.quote: You bring Watsi into your world in a way that feels authentic, in a way that feels like you. That can be pretty powerful and that's a way to help more people discover what Watsi is all about.

Kat reads slowly: the clean script runs about 2 minutes, not 70 s. For “shorter”, this plan drops the four “Maybe it starts…” lines (the first cut) and the “Our ambassadors each have a very different way” line. It runs about 1:50. For under 90 s, the next cut is the “There are a lot of different ways…” block (C5063 00:18–00:37). Never cut the four names or the button. Nick decides.
